newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RODRIGUEZ HITS FOR CYCLE AS MARINERS CRUSH TIGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RODRIGUEZ HITS FOR CYCLE AS MARINERS CRUSH TIGERS.

text.p: Alex Rodriguez performed a rare baseball feat Thursday when he hit for the cycle -- a single, double, triple and home run -- to lead the Seattle Mariners to a 14-6 romp over the Detroit Tigers.
Rodriguez homered in the first inning, singled in the fourth, tripled in the eighth and doubled in the ninth, accounting for four of Seattle 17 hits. He also has two RBI and scored three times.
"I'm excited, but I guess it hasn't really hit me yet," said Rodriguez.
"I'm only the second Mariner to do it, the other is Jay Buhner, who can't run," joked Rodriguez.
"First of all it's hard to get four hits in a game," said Seattle manager Lou Piniella. "This is only two in 21 years, that shows how hard it is (to hit for the cycle)."
Buhner, who hit his cycle in 1993, added a three-run homer and had four RBI and Dan Wilson and Russ Davis each contributed solo homers for Seattle.
Jeff Fassero (5-2) allowed three runs and five hits over seven innings for the win. Felipe Lira (4-3) was tagged for six runs and five hits in 3 1/3 innings for the loss.
In Milwaukee, Mo Vaughn's belted a two-run homer in the fourth inning and Tim Wakefield came within one out of a complete game as the Boston Red Sox nipped the Brewers 2-1.
With Wil Cordero on first, Vaughn smacked his 16th homer off Brewers starter Ben McDonald.
The Brewers got their lone run in the bottom of the inning on Mark Loretta's RBI single.

Wakefield (2-5) won for the first time since April 14, a span of five starts. He gave up one run on seven hits and struck out 10 in 8 2/3 innings. McDonald (6-4) allowed six hits in his first complete game of the season.

In Cleveland, Casey Candaele's one-out single to centre off Carlos Castillo in the bottom of the 11th inning scored Manny Ramirez with the winning run as the Indians edged the Chicago White Sox 5-4 to snap a four-game losing streak.
Omar Vizquel, who was 4-for-5 with a double, triple and an RBI, scored the tying run for the Indians in the eighth on Jim Thome's single.
Frank Thomas and Jorge Fabregas homered for Chicago off Cleveland starter Charles Nagy.
Paul Shuey (2-1) pitched a scoreless 11th to pick up the win for the Indians. Castillo (0-1) took the loss.
In Toronto, Jose Canseco hit a three-run homer in the eighth inning off Cy Young Award winner Pat Hentgen as the Oakland Athletics edged the Blue Jays 4-3.
Canseco sent a 2-2 pitch 417 feet into the left-field seats for his 12th home run of the season, scoring Geronimo Berroa and pinch-runner Damon Mashore to turn a two-run deficit into a 4-3 advantage.
Carlos Reyes (1-0) picked up the victory. Loser Hentgen (4-3) allowed four runs and seven hits in eight innings.
In Kansas City, Dean Palmer's run-scoring single snapped an 11th-inning tie and John Wetteland pitched 3 2/3 scoreless innings to lead the Texas Rangers to a 6-3 win over the Royals.
Palmer's bloop single to right off Hipolito Pichardo (1-2) scored Rusty Geer. The Rangers added a pair of insurance runs on Damon Buford's RBI single and Benji Gil's sacrifice fly.
Wetteland (3-0) allowed one hit and struck out three in his longest outing of the season. Pichardo allowed three runs and three hits and a walk in 1 1/3 innings.

At Minnesota, rookie Jason Dickson and Troy Percival combined on a six-hitter and Luis Alicea's two-out single in the seventh snapped a scoreless tie as the surging Anaheim Angels blanked the Twins 3-0.
Dickson (7-2) allowed just six singles and walked none, before giving way to Percival, who tossed a perfect ninth.
Alicea's two-out single to centre off Twins starter Bob Tewksbury scored Garret Anderson in the seventh and Anaheim, winner of 17 of its last 23, added two runs in the eighth.
Tewksbury (2-6), who retired the first 14 batters he faced, allowed three runs and nine hits.
